title: Unsupervised learning separates temporal expression components in synchronized HeLa cells
summary: The authors reanalyzed a public RNA-seq time course of synchronized HeLa cells after release from cell-cycle arrest. Fourier analysis and topic modeling separated two oscillatory components associated with G1–S and G2–M phases and a transient component associated with immediate-early response and proliferation. This is a computational interpretation of existing data, without independent experimental validation; the associations do not establish causal mechanisms.
ai_technology: Unsupervised topic modeling with Fourier analysis

evidence.tested: Unsupervised topic modeling and Fourier analysis were applied to a public time-course RNA-seq dataset from synchronized HeLa cells; the article reports three temporal components.
evidence.unknown: The study reanalyzes existing data and does not report independent experimental validation of the component interpretations.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised topic modeling decomposed time-dependent gene-expression measurements into latent temporal components, with Fourier analysis characterizing their patterns.
